links.outcome: Correct-answer rate of web-RAG LLMs with vs without whitelisting retrieval to authoritative neurology domains
links.effect: Correct rates open vs whitelisted: Sonar 60% vs 78%, Sonar-Pro 80% vs 88%, Sonar-Reasoning-Pro 81% vs 89%; mean accuracy gains 0.23, 0.08, 0.08 on 0-2 scale.
links.quote: Restricting retrieval to authoritative neurology domains yielded a clinically meaningful 8 to 18 percentage-point gain in correctness and halved output variability, upgrading a consumer search assistant to a decision-support-level tool that at least performed on par with a specialized literature engine.

unlisted_practices: Restricting web retrieval to whitelisted authoritative domains (source control) for RAG LLMs

screen.reason: The study directly tests a specific guardrail/deployment practice (domain whitelisting vs open-web retrieval for RAG-enabled LLMs) on clinical neurology question answering to see if it improves accuracy and safety.
